items.title: The Gulf’s emerging web of security partnerships
items.description: The signing of the Badr Memorandum of Understanding by Pakistan, Türkiye, Qatar and Indonesia in Doha on Wednesday is the latest manifestation of Middle Eastern states accelerated efforts for diversifying their defense partnerships amid growing doubts about the reliability of existing security arrangements of the region led by the United States. But, rather than laying the foundations of a new regional security architecture, the proliferation of such agreements is producing a more fractured landscape in which countries are drawing in more partners, pursuing separate strategic interests and accepting varying levels of military commitments. There could not be a bigger example of how uneven is the process than the agreements being signed up by regional countries themselves. Badr , for instance, focuses on defense manufacturing, technology transfer, research and development, and training, allowing its participants to pool industrial capabilities without committing themselves to military assistance in the event of an attack. In contrast the Makkah Joint Defense Agreement , concluded in August by Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkiye, goes considerably further by providing that an attack on one participant will be treated as an attack on all as it builds on a bilateral Strategic Mutual Defense Agreement between Pakistan and KSA signed in Sept 2025. These are two major agreements in addition to several others being signed or solidified by the countries in the region, but the contrast between Badr and Makkah agreements is telling because these agreements are often taken as evidence of an emerging regional security architecture, although the arrangements differ considerably in their purpose and obligations. Makkah agreement formalises security guarantees between participating countries, while Badr aims to develop industrial capacity. The momentum behind these regional security initiatives has grown since this year’s US - Israel war with Iran exposed the risks of relying heavily on external protection. For Gulf states in particular, the Iran conflict raised questions about whether existing security partnerships could adequately protect their interests during a major regional confrontation. Importantly, the response of the affected countries has not been to abandon US, whose military capabilities are still considered indispensable, but to seek additional options through new partnerships, domestic defense production and selective commitments. Besides the impression of the inadequacy of US security umbrella, this search for greater strategic autonomy also needs to be looked at in the context of the Gulf Cooperation Council’s own Joint Defense Agreement, signed in 2000, which too provides that aggression against one member constitutes aggression against all, yet the bloc has struggled to translate this commitment into an integrated military capability because of differences in equipment, command systems and national priorities. The hurdles to full operationalisation of Peninsula Shield Force has further exposed the gap between a collective defense principle and the ability to organise a coordinated response. The newer arrangements that the countries in the region are signing up partly reflect this GCC experience. Therefore, while these countries want enhanced security cooperation, they are also reluctant to surrender the freedom to make independent decisions. As a result, a network of partnerships is emerging that may complement one another in some areas without actually adding up to a common defense system. Pakistan’s expanding role illustrates both the opportunities and the limitations of this approach. Its relationship with Saudi Arabia has acquired a more formal security dimension through the 2025 bilateral agreement and the subsequent Makkah framework, while cooperation with Turkiye offers scope for closer military coordination and defense industrial collaboration. Egypt, another key player in the Arab world, has stayed outside the Makkah framework and has offered defense cooperation to Saudi Arabia, reflecting its interest in protecting its own regional priorities without becoming committed to a wider military confrontation. Islamabad’s other Gulf relationships, however, remain more limited in scope. Kuwait has strengthened defense cooperation with Pakistan through an upgraded agreement - the Protocol Agreement 2026 - covering training, capacity building and border management, while Bahrain has developed close links with the Pakistani military through the presence of Pakistani personnel in its National Guard and Coast Guard, alongside cooperation in training and logistics. These relationships have provided a basis for continued military engagement but do not carry the mutual defense obligations associated with the Pakistan - KSA partnership. Ties with UAE have, meanwhile, followed a more complicated course marred by political and financial strains, Islamabad’s closer alignment with Riyadh and Abu Dhabi’s expanding defense relationship with India. Nevertheless, training, personnel exchanges, counterterrorism activities and joint exercises between the two countries continue. Qatar has signed a defense industrial cooperation agreement involving Pakistan among others while Oman has maintained selective military ties with Pakistan and Turkiye, simultaneously preserving its wider security relationships and avoiding binding mutual defense commitments, consistent with its preference for neutrality and diplomatic engagement, particularly in relation to Iran and the Strait of Hormuz. This makes it difficult to describe Pakistan’s growing defense relationships as a unified regional bloc. Moreover, commitments under these agreements vary according to the interests and calculations of individual partners. Islamabad, in this situation, is left to balance closer security ties against its available military resources and the risk of becoming involved in conflicts whose objectives may not coincide with its own. At the same time the Gulf states are also pursuing different courses. Saudi Arabia is strengthening its relationships with Pakistan and Turkiye while continuing to rely on Western military capabilities and Egypt and exploring defense industrial cooperation with China. The UAE, which has not joined either the Makkah or Badr frameworks, has deepened security cooperation with Israel, including in air defense and counter drone capabilities, while maintaining close relationships with US, France and India. Qatar is seeking to expand its defense industrial partnerships through Badr but at the same time retains US military presence at Al Udeid. Bahrain remains closely aligned with Saudi Arabia and the GCC defense framework, while Kuwait continues to prioritise bilateral military cooperation with Pakistan alongside its substantial security relationship with Washington. Oman’s preference for neutrality and mediation further distinguishes its approach from those seeking more formal security commitments. The differences are not only confined to the choice of partners, but the states also have divergent assessments of the threat posed by Iran, the role of Israel in regional security and the degree to which they should commit themselves to one another’s defense. Their partnerships are therefore being shaped as much by the need to preserve freedom of action as by the desire to develop collective capabilities. The new partnerships do not either automatically translate into military independence for regional states, which continue to operate substantial inventories of Western origin aircraft, air defense systems and other advanced platforms that require specialised maintenance, software support, spare parts and replacement munitions. New partners may help diversify procurement and develop local production, but they cannot necessarily replace established suppliers on the required scale. Moreover, addition of newer systems can also complicate logistics and interoperability unless countries invest in common procedures, training and secure communications. Defense industrial cooperation presents another challenge and agreements such as Badr will acquire practical significance only if they lead to funded production programs, meaningful technology transfer and capabilities that participating countries can maintain and sustain. Similarly, the credibility of mutual defense arrangements will depend on whether their members can coordinate intelligence, plan jointly and establish procedures for responding to a crisis. The number of agreements signed, therefore, is less important than the military capabilities and obligations they actually produce. For Washington, this proliferation of new defense agreements may apparently look like a challenge, but this should definitely not be seen as it being replaced. US undoubtedly remains deeply embedded in the region through military bases, intelligence cooperation, arms sales and longstanding defense relationships. The emerging shift may, however, give the regional countries greater bargaining power with established suppliers, particularly as they press for domestic production, technology partnerships and greater control over maintenance and supply chains. To put it simply the emerging arrangements are an attempt to manage the uncertainty created by recent geo-political developments especially the receding US footprint rather than replace the existing system outright. The central contradiction in the Gulf countries response to the emerging situation, however, is that while these states are seeking greater security through a proliferation of partnerships, they remain unwilling, or unable, to reconcile their differences over the threats they face and the obligations they are prepared to assume.

items.title: Arachide, riz, coton : les filières agricoles au cœur du plan gouvernemental
items.description: Écoulement des stocks d’arachide, compétitivité du riz local, relance du coton et nouveaux débouchés pour les céréales et les produits horticoles : le Conseil interministériel du 22 octobre a arrêté des mesures spécifiques pour soutenir les différentes filières et améliorer la commercialisation des productions nationales. Le Gouvernement veut apporter des réponses différenciées aux difficultés rencontrées par les filières agricoles. Lors du Conseil interministériel consacré à la campagne 2026-2027, il a fixé des orientations allant de la valorisation des stocks à la régulation des importations, en passant par le financement des achats et l’organisation des circuits de commercialisation. Arachide : écouler les stocks et préparer la collecte Pour la filière arachidière, l’un des enjeux concerne les 70 450 tonnes de tourteaux détenues par la SONACOS. Le Gouvernement prévoit de diversifier les débouchés, notamment par la vente aux fabricants d’aliments pour bétail et aux meuniers, à un prix révisé. Une partie du stock doit également contribuer à l’assistance pastorale prévue pour la soudure 2026, dont les besoins en aliments de bétail sont estimés à 14 706 tonnes. La SONACOS est par ailleurs appelée à valoriser son patrimoine foncier afin de financer le renouvellement de ses anciennes lignes industrielles, de diversifier ses produits finis et de renforcer ses fonds propres. Pour la nouvelle campagne, le dispositif prévoit aussi un comité chargé de recommander chaque année un prix de l’arachide conciliant protection des producteurs et compétitivité à l’exportation. Riz local : améliorer l’écoulement et la compétitivité La situation du riz local appelle des mesures spécifiques. Au 13 octobre 2026, 13 879 tonnes de riz blanc avaient été enlevées sur un stock disponible de 41 729 tonnes. Le Gouvernement prévoit de mettre en œuvre un mécanisme de péréquation liant les importations aux achats de riz local et de payer aux riziers la subvention de 50 FCFA par kilogramme due sur les quantités déjà enlevées. Les autorités veulent également faire reconnaître l’interprofession réunissant producteurs, riziers et importateurs, sécuriser les stocks des rizeries grâce à la tierce détention et harmoniser les emballages, la qualité et la marque du riz local. Une stratégie de renforcement de sa compétitivité devra être élaborée avant la fin de l’année. Un atelier entre le Comité interprofessionnel riz du Sénégal et la Banque Agricole est aussi prévu avant l’ouverture de la campagne pour préparer le financement de 2027. Coton, maïs et productions diversifiées La relance du coton doit se poursuivre avec un objectif de production de 35 000 tonnes et un paiement des producteurs dans un délai de trois jours. L’enveloppe de soutien de 5 milliards de FCFA doit être confirmée avant le 15 novembre 2026. Le Gouvernement souhaite aussi associer des acheteurs industriels à la commercialisation et organiser la valorisation de la graine de coton par les huileries et les fabricants d’aliments pour bétail. Pour le maïs, le protocole entre l’État et les fabricants d’aliments pour bétail doit être renouvelé autour d’un objectif de 30 000 tonnes, avec un accompagnement bancaire. Dans l’horticulture, les autorisations d’importation seront liées à la disponibilité effective de la production nationale et à la justification d’achats locaux. Le fonds de commercialisation de l’oignon et de la pomme de terre doit être renforcé. Enfin, l’approche des protocoles de commercialisation sera étendue au mil et au sésame, avec des objectifs respectifs de 150 000 et 50 000 tonnes. Leurs besoins de financement devront être estimés et suivis chaque semaine, au même titre que ceux du riz local et des produits horticoles. À travers ces mesures, le Gouvernement cherche à mieux organiser les débouchés, à soutenir les producteurs et à réduire les difficultés d’écoulement des productions nationales. C.G. DIOP

items.title: Ukraine says Starlink still restricted after Trump says limits lifted
items.description: Ukraine is still recording issues with the Starlink network, sources within the defence ministry say, after Donald Trump said limits on the satellite uplink had been reversed by Elon Musk. The sources told the BBC that instances of drones experiencing connection loss at speeds of 161km/h (100mph) were being recorded, hampering military operations. The US president had denied instructing the tech billionaire to restrict connectivity to Starlink’s military-grade counterpart, Starshield, before saying on Thursday that Musk had “put it back”. Musk previously said he was not behind the slowdown, which affected Ukraine’s ability to use attack drones and co-ordinate defensive operations. The Ukrainian defence ministry sources said the military was constantly monitoring the performance of both the Starlink and Starshield networks. They added that there was “currently no confirmation that these restrictions have been lifted”. Last week, Kyiv said uplink speeds to the low Earth orbit satellites had been restricted, affecting the speed at which drones could travel. Any drone travelling faster than 100mph lost its connection, officials said. Shortly after, Musk said that Starshield, which Ukraine uses for some of its operation, was controlled by the US military and suggested that the Pentagon could be behind the issues. The White House has since repeatedly denied deliberately placing limits on the network in Ukraine. Trump refused to say whether he had called Musk to ask him to liftrestrictions to the service when asked about reports to that end on Thursday, but said: “Bottom line, he put it back.” Ukraine uses both the civilian service Starlink and the more secure Starshield, depending on what communications are needed. The networks use 10,000 satellites to provide connectivity, particularly in remote areas and on the battlefield. Starshield allows Ukrainian drone operators to see targets in real time, as well as operate interceptor drones. Russia is not authorised to use Starlink, so when Ukraine sends long-range missiles deep into Russia to hit oil refineries, the network does not work. Ukrainian reports of a slowdown to the service came during a tense diplomatic row between Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky about Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil infrastructure. Faced with midterm elections next month, Trump has waived some sanctions on Russia and agreed a deal to import Russian diesel for the US market – a move criticised by Ukraine and its European allies. Trump said the strikes on Russian oil refineries, which Kyiv says are crucial to stemming the main revenue source for Moscow’s war effort, have pushed global prices higher. While the attacks have had an impact on global fuel prices, rises seen this year have primarily been due to the Iran war. Zelensky said the US had also threatened to withdraw intelligence sharing if the strikes did not stop, something Trump later denied. The row prompted a war of words between the two world leaders, with Trump suggesting it was time for Ukraine to get a new president and Zelensky implying Trump was not a real leader. Earlier on Thursday – before Trump’s comments – Zelensky had said the speed of the system had still not been restored fully. “I am waiting to hear from US Secretary of State [Marco] Rubio. He promised to get back to me with information within 48 hours or so.” The Wall Street Journal reported that Trump had told Musk that he was frustrated the Starlink system’s speeds were still capped, and that the system was working closer to normal following that conversation.

items.title: US Conference of Catholic Bishops says not linked to Trump prayer event
items.description: The United States Conference of Catholic Bishops on Thursday told AFP it was not linked to a group seen in a video praying with President Donald Trump in the Oval Office. “This was not something that the USCCB organized. It is not affiliated with the Conference. I have no further information,” said a spokesperson for the organization, Chieko Noguchi, to AFP. On Thursday an aide to the US president, Margo Martin, shared a video showing the president seated at his desk, flanked by clergy wearing collars. One had his hand on the president’s shoulder and prayed aloud. “Catholic Archbishops and Bishops pray with President Trump in the Oval Office,” captioned Martin in her post on X, including a heart emoji. The White House later confirmed to AFP that the president had met with a dozen Catholic faith leaders, including the archbishops of Denver, Milwaukee and Kansas City. The Trump administration’s relationship with the Catholic Church has been fraught, particularly regarding the policy of deporting migrants. Trump, who enjoyed support from the Christian right during his most recent presidential campaign, has held several prayer gatherings similar to Thursday’s event, including with evangelical pastors. AFP The post US Conference of Catholic Bishops says not linked to Trump prayer event appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Saint-Louis: l’Aser mise sur le solaire pour électrifier les villages isolés
items.description: En tournée à Saint-Louis, jeudi 22 octobre, le directeur général de l’Agence sénégalaise d’électrification rurale (Aser), Pape Momar Ngom a visité les installations solaires de Bouh Minguene et de Khelcom Diaw, dans la commune de Gandon. L’objectif est d’évaluer ces équipements et de renforcer les solutions d’accès à l’électricité dans les villages enclavés, en vue de l’électrification universelle à l’horizon 2029 Nommé le 1er octobre dernier, le nouveau directeur général de l’Aser a entamé sa tournée nationale par la région de Saint-Louis. Accompagné de représentants de Compagnie marroco-sénégalaise d'électricité (Comasel) concessionnaire de la zone, il a rencontré les populations pour recueillir leurs appréciations sur les installations solaires mises en place et identifier les difficultés rencontrées. Pape Momar Ngom a notamment salué l’intérêt des kits solaires individuels pour les localités où l’habitat est dispersé et où le raccordement au réseau électrique classique est coûteux. « Nous avons décidé de visiter ces installations pour voir comment démultiplier cette solution dans d’autres localités qui présentent des configurations similaires », a-t-il expliqué. Pour atteindre l’accès universel à l’électricité avant 2029, l’Aser prévoit trois approches notamment l’extension du réseau existant pour les villages proches des lignes électriques, la construction de centrales solaires avec un réseau de distribution pour les localités plus importantes et l’installation de kits individuels dans les villages les plus dispersés. 6 471 villages encore à électrifier et 400 milliards recherchés Ces équipements permettent notamment l’éclairage, la ventilation et l’utilisation de téléviseurs et de réfrigérateurs. Ils peuvent également améliorer les conditions d’apprentissage des élèves et faciliter la conservation des médicaments dans les structures sanitaires adaptées. « Les Sénégalais, où qu’ils se trouvent, ont droit à l’électricité », a affirmé le directeur général. Selon Pape Momar Ngom, 6 471 villages restent à couvrir dans le cadre des efforts engagés. Les besoins de financement sont estimés à 400 milliards de FCfa, en complément des projets en cours. Une table ronde avec les bailleurs a permis selon lui, de recueillir plus de 800 milliards de FCfa de promesses de financement, dont les conditions doivent encore être examinées. La tournée a également été marquée par une rencontre avec le préfet de Saint-Louis. Le directeur général a insisté sur la nécessité d’associer les autorités administratives à la mise en œuvre des programmes. « On ne peut pas faire des programmes de l’État sans passer par les autorités administratives », a-t-il souligné, rappelant que l’électricité constitue un service social de base essentiel à l’amélioration des conditions de vie des populations rurales. Jeanne SAGNA (Correspondante)

items.description: Auteur d’un superbe but lors de la victoire de l’Ajax Amsterdam face à l’Atalanta Bergame (2-0), jeudi en Ligue Conférence, le jeune Marocain Abdellah Ouazane confirme son potentiel à seulement 17 ans. Sa performance relance les discussions sur sa place en sélection nationale et sur la gestion de son temps de jeu par Mohamed Ouahbi. Abdellah Ouazane continue de faire parler de lui en Europe. Le jeune milieu offensif marocain s’est illustré jeudi soir avec l’Ajax Amsterdam en inscrivant un but spectaculaire lors du succès de son équipe contre l’Atalanta Bergame (2-0), en Ligue Conférence. Entré en cours de jeu, le joueur de 17 ans a signé une réalisation de grande classe dans le temps additionnel, à la 90e+3 minute. Après avoir éliminé Raoul Bellanova sur le côté droit de la surface, il a déclenché une frappe puissante dans un angle fermé, envoyant le ballon sous la barre après un rebond sur le poteau. Cette performance confirme les qualités techniques du jeune international marocain et attire de nouveau l’attention sur son évolution, aussi bien en club qu’en sélection. Les performances d’Ouazane avec l’Ajax relancent le débat autour de son utilisation par Mohamed Ouahbi lors du rassemblement d’octobre avec les Lions de l’Atlas. Pour sa première convocation avec l’équipe nationale A, le jeune joueur n’avait disputé que 15 minutes lors de la rencontre face au Gabon, remportée par le Maroc sur le score de 2-0. Il était ensuite resté sur le banc contre le Lesotho, avant de ne pas entrer en jeu lors du match amical face au Mali. Cette gestion avait suscité des critiques de la part de certains supporters, désireux de voir davantage à l’œuvre l’un des jeunes talents les plus prometteurs du football marocain. Son but face à l’Atalanta pourrait ainsi alimenter les discussions à l’approche du prochain rassemblement de novembre. Un talent à accompagner progressivement Si le potentiel d’Abdellah Ouazane ne fait pas débat, son intégration doit néanmoins s’inscrire dans la durée. À l’Ajax, le joueur n’est pas encore un titulaire régulier : en neuf apparitions en championnat néerlandais cette saison, il n’a débuté que deux rencontres. Son premier rassemblement avec les A constitue également un élément important à prendre en compte. À seulement 17 ans, il doit encore s’adapter aux exigences du haut niveau international et gagner progressivement sa place au sein d’un groupe où la concurrence reste importante. Son exploit européen témoigne de ses qualités et de sa capacité à faire la différence, mais ne suffit pas, à lui seul, à remettre en cause la hiérarchie établie par le sélectionneur. Le prochain rassemblement permettra d’observer si Mohamed Ouahbi choisit de lui accorder davantage de responsabilités ou de poursuivre son intégration progressive. The post Abdellah Ouazane brille avec l’Ajax et relance le débat sur son temps de jeu avec les Lions de l’Atlas appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Five Israelis wounded and two suspected Palestinian attackers killed in West Bank shooting
items.description: Five Israelis have been wounded and two suspected Palestinian attackers killed by Israeli security forces following a shooting in the occupied West Bank, Israeli officials say. Footage verified by the BBC shows an intense gun battle between soldiers and the gunmen, at a military checkpoint at the entrance to the city of Hebron. In response, Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he had ordered the military to prepare for a full lockdown of the West Bank, beginning later on Friday. The attack comes at a time of high tensions, with extremist Jewish settlers targeting Palestinians during the annual olive harvest, and Israel’s general election taking place in four days time. The two injured Israelis are in critical condition, according to Israel’s ambulance service. The Israeli military said it had found a large quantity of ammunition in the attackers’ vehicle. The military said they believe the gunmen had intended to carry out a much larger attack on the nearby Route 35, but ran into the checkpoint – so instead decided to open fire there. Unverified CCTV footage shows two gunmen exit a car armed with what appears to be a handgun and an assault rifle and start firing on soldiers at the checkpoint, before coming under return fire. The Israeli military said it had begun raids on the homes of the attackers, while far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich said he had ordered the demolition of several Palestinian buildings adjacent to the site of the attack. It is common practice for Israeli forces to demolish the homes of Palestinians who are suspected of carrying out attacks on Israelis. Netanyahu, who has built his election campaign on promising security for Israelis, said that his Likud party would cancel campaign events for the morning. The West Bank was already expected to be placed under lockdown for the election on Monday and Tuesday, according to Israeli media. At least 96 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli forces or settlers in the West Bank since the start of the year, according to the UN. Four Israelis, both security forces and civilians, have been killed by Palestinians there over the same period, the UN says.

items.title: Yelen : La plateforme qui met les petits commerçants francophones en ligne
items.description: © Internet Vendre sur WhatsApp, Tiktok ou Instagram est devenu courant en Afrique francophone, mais encaisser les paiements et suivre les commandes reste compliqué. C’est de ce constat qu’est née Yelen, une jeune entreprise lancée en juin 2025 par Ibrahima Sylla, avec son cofondateur Christian Okoth. L’idée est venue de conversations avec des vendeurs qui évoquaient leurs difficultés à encaisser leurs paiements et à gérer leurs ventes entre WhatsApp, Tiktok et Instagram. Yelen propose donc de créer une boutique en ligne sans écrire une ligne de code. Le besoin est réel. En Afrique francophone, les PME représentent plus de 90% des entreprises, mais moins de la moitié vendent en ligne, selon TechCabal. Pour la livraison, les commerçants gèrent eux-mêmes les envois locaux, tandis que l’expédition internationale passe par un partenariat avec DHL. La plateforme prend aussi en charge les paiements mobiles transfrontaliers et s’intègre aux systèmes de paiement locaux, un gage de confiance pour les acheteurs comme pour les vendeurs. Son modèle économique combine abonnements et frais sur les transactions. Les premiers résultats sont encourageants. Depuis son lancement, Yelen affirme avoir intégré plus de 3 000 vendeurs et traité environ 40 000 dollars de transactions. Elle s’appuie surtout sur la Côte d’Ivoire, où le commerce en ligne a généré 534 millions de dollars de revenus en 2024 et où se concentrent 70% de ses utilisateurs. Selon Techpoint Africa, la start-up opère dans des régions francophones comme le Sénégal, le Cameroun, le Togo, le Mali, le Bénin, le Niger et le Gabon, et ses utilisateurs se répartissent sur dix marchés, dont la République démocratique du Congo. Ibrahima Sylla n’en est pas à son premier projet. Techpoint Africa le présente comme un ancien de Google et d’Anka, et rapporte qu’un produit précédent avait gagné une certaine traction avant qu’il ne juge le marché pas prêt. Le média décrit Yelen comme un Shopify pour les vendeurs des réseaux sociaux, mais le fondateur assure que la plateforme s’en distingue fondamentalement. Son ambition affichée est de devenir l’infrastructure du commerce en ligne pour les vendeurs sociaux. Dans une région où le commerce passe beaucoup par les discussions en ligne, Yelen entend bâtir les rails qui soutiendront la croissance du secteur. Ibrahim Baby

items.title: No electricity, no vote, South Africans threaten to shun ANC
items.description: Thick cables snaked along footpaths in a township outside South Africa’s wealthiest city, Johannesburg, where 180 households have relied on illegal electricity connections for more than 20 years. Angry about the authorities’ failure to get them properly connected to the grid, residents have resolved to turn their backs on their ANC-led municipality at the November 4 local elections, a test for the once-majority party that has been bleeding support for more than two decades. “We have made a collective decision: no electricity, no vote,” said community leader Lesiba Rankapole, 59. For other communities across the country, complaints feeding disillusionment with African National Congress (ANC) municipalities include failures to provide water or collect garbage, as well as mismanagement and corruption. “We know it is illegal, but we had no choice because we cannot live without electricity,” said Rankapole of the wires that take power from another area of Katlehong, a sprawling semi-urban area on the edge of Johannesburg. “Our children cannot progress without electricity.” It is “obvious we are not going to vote, especially for the ANC”, said another resident, Enock Majola, 57, who pointed out illegal dumping sites. “I was born ANC, but today I do not want anyone to tell me about the ANC because I am suffering,” he said. – Sliding support – At the heart of South Africa’s anti-apartheid struggle, the ANC — the party of jailed liberation hero-turned-president Nelson Mandela — took nearly 70 percent of the national vote in 2004. It fell below 50 percent for the first time at the last municipal elections in 2021, when it won 46 percent of votes and retained control of nearly half the municipalities. At the 2024 national vote, it managed just over 40 percent and was forced to accept a coalition government. The party’s weakness has emboldened spin-offs such as the uMkhonto weSizwe Party (MKP) led by former president Jacob Zuma that is contesting local elections for the first time this year. Elsewhere in Katlehong, Meshack Twala was digging to reach a blocked pipe at a house surrounded by sewage. “How do we go and vote when our entire street has been experiencing persistent sewage problems?” he said, conceding, though, that if he did make it to a voting station, he would plump for the ANC. “Changing to other parties would not feel right,” the 58-year-old said. Municipal elections generally attract low turnout, which “hurts the ANC”, said political analyst Sethulego Matebesi. But the vote will give parties an “idea of where their support base is” as they look towards the 2029 national poll, he said. Matebesi predicted no party would win an outright majority and the country would be “full swing” into coalition-building and hung municipalities. – Johannesburg: the big prize – Of the 257 councils up for grabs, the fight for control is particularly intense in Johannesburg, an economic dynamo of more than 4.8 million people and the face of Africa’s most industrialised nation. South Africa’s stark inequalities are laid bare in the Alexandra township from where skyscrapers of the Sandton business district — reputed to be the richest square mile on the continent — are visible. Heaps of rubbish, potholes and sewage flows lined the roads. “The ANC has been governing for years, but we have not seen any changes in Alexandra,” said maintenance worker Patrick Saohatse, 45. He said he would give his vote to the liberal Democratic Alliance, the second-largest party in the ruling coalition after the ANC. Already in charge of the country’s second city Cape Town, the DA has pushed hard on ANC service delivery failures and mismanagement in a campaign that started more than a year ago. “Another five years of corruption and collapsing infrastructure will push our city beyond recovery,” said mayoral candidate, 75-year-old Helen Zille, at a recent rally. Less than two weeks before polling day, the ANC was yet to choose its candidate amid lacklustre campaigning. “If you look at the situation in and around Johannesburg, there are reasons for people not to be happy,” the party’s head of elections, Mdumiseni Ntuli, told AFP. “We have made mistakes and accepted our shortcomings, but ANC remains a better option for people,” he said, urging voters to cast their ballots. Running for a second chance to be Johannesburg mayor is the leader of the centre-right Action SA, Herman Mashaba, 67. “Our refuse collection is irregular; our streets have no lights… I keep asking myself, what on earth is happening?” he said to AFP. items.title: South-East has better presidential options than Peter Obi – Umahi
items.description: Nigeria’s Minister of Works, David Umahi, has said Peter Obi is not the best presidential candidate the South-East can produce, arguing that the former Anambra State governor failed to consult regional political leaders before pursuing his 2023 presidential ambition. Umahi made the remarks in an interview with Arise News and insisted his stance on Peter Obi’s candidacy was not driven by personal differences with Obi, but by his belief that the Southeast has other qualified political figures capable of seeking the presidency. “Peter Obi is not the best of our finest in South-East,” Umahi said. “He’s not the best; he can never be the best.” The former Ebonyi State governor argued that anyone seeking to represent the political interests of the South-East at the national level should first engage governors and other influential stakeholders in the region to build consensus. “You cannot play politics in South-East without consulting people like us,” he said. Umahi added that if he were seeking the presidency, he would consult widely with political leaders before declaring his ambition, stressing that such a move should not be undertaken without engaging those whose interests the candidate claims to represent. He also challenged the perception that Obi should automatically be considered the South-East’s strongest presidential option because of his performance in the 2023 election. According to him, the region has several qualified politicians who should be considered in future discussions about producing Nigeria’s president. The minister further argued that the presidency should not automatically be allocated to Anambra State whenever the South-East gets an opportunity to produce a president. He noted that Nigeria’s first president, Nnamdi Azikiwe, hailed from the area that now forms Anambra State, adding that Ebonyi, Enugu, Abia and Imo should also be considered. Umahi’s comments came amid growing political discussions ahead of the 2027 presidential election, particularly over support for President Bola Tinubu among political leaders in the South-East. Umahi defended those backing Tinubu, rejecting suggestions that their political choices amounted to a betrayal of the region. He maintained that the South-East could improve its chances of producing a president through negotiations and alliances with other parts of the country rather than treating support for any individual politician as a measure of regional loyalty. ‘Keep this team for the future’ – Kassim Ocansey tells GFA
items.description: Black Starlets head coach Kassim Ocansey has urged the Ghana Football Association (GFA) to keep the current U17 squad together, stressing that consistency and continuity will be crucial to developing a strong foundation for the senior national teams. Ocansey believes the young players have demonstrated significant potential at the 2026 WAFU Zone B U17 Championship in Burkina Faso and should be given the opportunity to develop together rather than being disbanded after the tournament. “I will say we should not do away with the team. We must keep this team together for the future. There are a lot of potential players in the team and if we can keep them, they can be the foundation for the future of our senior national teams.” The coach’s appeal highlights the importance of long-term planning in Ghanaian football, where promising young players need a clear pathway from youth football to the senior level. Maintaining the core of a squad over time can help players build stronger partnerships, gain valuable international experience and adapt to the demands of competitive football. Ocansey’s call goes beyond preserving a single squad. It is a plea for a consistent development strategy that gives talented youngsters the time and support they need to mature into senior internationals. With the right investment and continuity, members of the current Black Starlets team could form an important part of Ghana’s future at the highest level.

items.title: Macron reçoit les lycéens et fait face à un recours devant le Conseil d’État
items.description: Critique pour s'etre tenu a distance durant un mois de crise marquee par des violences , le chef de l'etat accelere. Il recoit ce 23 octobre a 15 heures les representants des organisations lyceennes, une premiere depuis le debut de la contestation. Cette initiative survient alors qu'un recours a ete depose devant le Conseil d'etat contre ses propos limitant les corteges non syndicaux samedi. Une tentative de dialogue sous haute tension Le president Emmanuel Macron grille la priorite au Premier ministre Sebastien Lecornu, qui doit rencontrer les lyceens et d'autres acteurs le 26 octobre. « Nous lui presenterons nos revendications qui sont toujours les memes », a confie Nathanael Combary, president du Renouveau lyceen et adherent du parti presidentiel, qui evoque le bâti scolaire et Parcoursup. D'autres se montrent plus sceptiques. Pierre Sourzat, president de l'organisation Les Lyceens, estime qu'« il va nous ecouter, il va faire semblant de nous avoir compris et puis apres il n'y aura pas de suite ». Sur franceinfo, l'eurodeputee de La France insoumise Manon Aubry a declare : « Je me demande ce que le pouvoir attend pour donner suite aux revendications lyceennes » et « j'ai envie de dire il etait temps ». 🔴 🗣 "Je me demande ce que le pouvoir attend pour donner suite aux revendications lycéennes", déclare l'eurodéputée LFI Manon Aubry, alors qu'Emmanuel Macron reçoit aujourd'hui à partir de 15h les représentants lycéens. "J'ai envie de dire il était temps", ajoute-t-elle. #canal16 — franceinfo (@franceinfo) October 23, 2026 Les organisations tiendront un point presse a la sortie de la reunion. Le chef de l'etat presidera aussi un conseil de defense ou des decisions securitaires supplementaires sont attendues. Le gouvernement a deja annonce le renforcement des effectifs de 20 % par rapport au 17 octobre . Seules les manifestations syndicales seront autorisees le 24 octobre, selon la « recommandation generale » de Macron. Lyon, Marseille et d'autres villes ont interdit des rassemblements. L'Association de defense des libertes constitutionnelles et le Syndicat de la magistrature ont depose un refere-liberte devant le Conseil d'etat. Manon Lefebvre, secretaire nationale du syndicat, s'inquiete des limitations du droit de manifester annoncees par Macron : « Ce qui nous choque, c'est la notion de legitimite. » Manifestations non syndicales interdites le 24 octobre: "Ce qui nous choque, c'est la notion de légitimité" des manifestants, explique Manon Lefebvre, secrétaire nationale du Syndicat de la Magistrature https://t.co/pGT0PEvWwA — BFM (@BFMTV) October 22, 2026 Les deux requerants contestent une atteinte au droit de manifester et un possible abus de pouvoir. Ils n'avaient en revanche pas defendu ce droit lorsque le pouvoir en place avait interdit l'hommage nationaliste du 9 mai. Des organisations etudiantes comme la Federation des associations generales etudiantes, l'Union nationale des etudiants de France et l'Union etudiante reclament aussi d'etre entendues sur leurs mesures chiffrees a dix milliards d'euros.

items.title: Lutte contre le blanchiment : le Cameroun veut restaurer la confiance des investisseurs
items.description: © DR Passé de 46% à près de 80% de réalisation de son plan d'action, le Cameroun veut finaliser les 5 dernières mesures exigées par le GAFI pour sortir de la surveillance renforcée et restaurer la confiance des investisseurs. Le compte à rebours est lancé.Le Comité national de coordination de la lutte contre le blanchiment de capitaux, le financement du terrorisme et la prolifération des armes de destruction massive a tenu sa deuxième session ordinaire de l'année, le 22 octobre 2026 à Yaoundé, sous la présidence du Ministre Délégué auprès du Ministre des Finances, Yaouba Abdoulaye. Les chiffres présentés sont encourageants. Le Cameroun est passé de 11 à 19 actions réalisées sur 24, faisant progresser son taux de réalisation de 46% à près de 80%, selon les rapports de suivi présentés au Groupe d'action financière (GAFI). L'enjeu est économique autant que réputationnel. Figurer sur la liste grise du GAFI coûte cher : coût du financement plus élevé, vigilance accrue des banques correspondantes, méfiance des investisseurs et ralentissement des flux financiers. Pour en sortir, les administrations concernées sont appelées à finaliser les 5 actions restantes, tandis que les efforts de contrôle et de supervision du secteur non financier doivent être renforcés. Cette session marque une nouvelle étape dans l'accélération des réformes engagées par le Gouvernement pour permettre au Cameroun de sortir de la surveillance renforcée du GAFI. Au-delà de la conformité, il s'agit de sécuriser le système financier national, de protéger l'attractivité du pays et de rassurer les partenaires économiques. Cet article Lutte contre le blanchiment : le Cameroun veut restaurer la confiance des investisseurs est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: World must cut emissions 18% in four years to find a way back below 1.5°C – UN 2026 Emissions Gap Report
items.description: Countries must slash greenhouse gas emissions by almost a fifth (18%) by 2030 and 45% by 2035, compared with 2025 levels. Only then can they stop global heating from running far past 1.5 degrees Celsius (°C) and bring it back down by the end of the century, the United Nations said on Wednesday. In its annual Emissions Gap Report , the UN Environment Programme (UNEP) said decades of weak action had made crossing 1.5°C “imminent and unavoidable”. If deep cuts start now, warming could peak at about 1.7–1.8°C around the middle of the century, with roughly an even chance of falling back to 1.5°C by 2100. “Overshoot is not surrender,” UN Secretary-General António Guterres said in a message on the report. “We can still keep it as small and as short as possible.” Under the 2015 Paris Agreement, almost every country promised to keep global warming “well below” 2°C and to try to stop it at 1.5°C. The figure measures the rise in Earth’s average temperature over many years, compared with the late 1800s, before factories and cars. UNEP now says that even if every country cut its emissions as hard as possible starting today, warming would still pass 1.5°C, because so much heat-trapping gas has already built up in the air. Scientists call this an overshoot: going above the limit for a while, likely for several decades, and then pulling temperatures back down. And on the policies governments actually have in place, the world is not heading for a small overshoot at all, but for about 2.8°C by 2100. Figure 1. Where warming is heading by 2100 under different paths. This is what climate change is. Burning coal, oil and gas, and clearing forests, releases carbon dioxide and other gases that trap the sun’s heat like a blanket. The thicker the blanket, the hotter the planet gets. Above 1.5°C, the report warns, heatwaves, floods and droughts become more frequent and severe, bringing more heat deaths and economic losses. Every extra fraction of a degree also raises the risk of changes that cannot be undone, such as melting ice sheets, carbon escaping from thawing frozen ground, disrupted ocean currents and the loss of coral reefs. Coming back down will take more than cutting pollution. About 320 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide, roughly eight years of today’s fossil fuel emissions, would have to be pulled back out of the air this century, and UNEP calls that uncertain. The effects are already visible. The EU’s Copernicus Climate Change Service said August 2026 tied July 2023 as the hottest month ever recorded, with an average global air temperature of 16.96°C, 1.65°C above pre-industrial levels. The world’s oceans were also the warmest ever measured for an August. The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) warned on Wednesday that the El Niño now building in the Pacific “could be unprecedented in strength”, and the UN says about 50 million people could face greater hunger as a result. The WMO also found that 2025 was one of Africa’s warmest years on record. Researchers at the University of Chicago’s Climate Impact Lab estimate that the extra heat from this El Niño alone could cause about 451,000 additional deaths worldwide between June 2026 and February 2027. Nigeria faces about 31,400 extra deaths between September and February, more than any other country. Looking further ahead, the lab projects that Sahel countries such as Niger and Burkina Faso could see 60 or more heat deaths for every 100,000 people each year by 2050, a higher rate than malaria causes in Africa today. Rising temperatures are also moving malaria itself. A study in Nature , promoted by the University of Chicago and co-written by Climate Impact Lab researchers, found that some very hot West African and Sahel countries are becoming too hot for malaria-carrying mosquitoes, while risk is climbing in the cooler highlands of East Africa and in southern Africa. By 2100 it could rise by about 20% in areas such as the Rift Valley. Table 1. The warming we are already living with What The numbers Source Hottest month on record (joint) August 2026: 16.96°C, 1.65°C above pre-industrial; ties July 2023 Copernicus, 10 Sept 2026 Ocean heat Warmest August sea surface ever measured: 21.07°C Copernicus, 10 Sept 2026 El Niño “Could be unprecedented in strength”; about 50 million could face more hunger WMO/OCHA briefing, 21 Oct 2026 Extra heat deaths from El Niño About 451,000 worldwide (June 2026–Feb 2027); Nigeria about 31,400 (Sept–Feb) UChicago Climate Impact Lab, Sept 2026 Heat deaths by 2050 60+ per 100,000 people a year in Sahel countries such as Niger and Burkina Faso Climate Impact Lab, Mar 2026 Africa 2025 was one of the continent’s warmest years on record WMO State of the Climate in Africa 2025 The outlook is bleaker than a year ago. UNEP’s 2025 report, Off target , said warming could still be held close to 1.5°C if emissions fell 26% by 2030 and 46% by 2035 from 2019 levels. This year’s edition, The point of return , says that chance “has been lost”. Even if every country kept its climate plan, emissions would fall only 5–8% by 2030, and warming would reach 2.6°C by 2100. Last year the same calculation gave 2.3–2.5°C. UNEP blamed the change mainly on the United States leaving the Paris Agreement and on revised estimates of past emissions. Global emissions reached 58.4 billion tonnes in 2025, roughly level with 2024, and every five years of pollution at today’s rate pushes peak warming up by about 0.1°C. Table 2. One year on: what changed between the 2025 and 2026 reports 2025 report: Off target 2026 report: The point of return Global emissions 57.7 billion tonnes in 2024, up 2.3% 58.4 billion tonnes in 2025, roughly flat 1.5°C goal Still within reach with a limited overshoot Chance with no or limited overshoot “has been lost”; peak 1.7–1.8°C Cuts needed 26% by 2030 and 46% by 2035 (vs 2019) 18% by 2030, 45% by 2035, 69% by 2040 (vs 2025) Warming if all pledges kept 2.3–2.5°C 2.6°C Warming on current policies Up to 2.8°C 2.8°C Countries with new climate plans 60 (63% of emissions) 124 (about 76% of emissions) Figure 2. Global emissions since 1990 and where different paths take them. “Every additional fraction of a degree and additional year of warming above 1.5°C increases climate impacts and risks,” said Inger Andersen, UNEP’s executive director. “So, we must pull out all the stops to minimize peak warming and return to 1.5°C by the end of the century.” Countries are moving, but slowly. By 1 September, 124 governments covering about 76% of global emissions had handed in new climate plans, up from 60 a year earlier. Every G20 member except Argentina, Saudi Arabia and the United States has now set targets for 2035, but only Mexico strengthened its target for 2030, and only six G20 members (China, India, Indonesia, Russia, South Africa and Türkiye) are on course to meet their 2030 goals. The Paris Agreement’s main tool for closing the gap is the global stocktake, a check-up every five years on whether countries are doing enough together. The first, completed at the COP28 summit in Dubai in 2023, set goals such as tripling renewable energy and moving away from fossil fuels. The second runs until 2028, and the report urges governments to use it to set clear goals for 2035 and 2040. Figure 3. The emissions gap: cuts needed versus cuts promised. The report spells out where the cuts must come from. Electricity from coal must fall by at least 75% by 2035 and 95% by 2040. The energy the world draws from coal, oil and gas must drop by 55%, 15% and 5% respectively by 2035. Methane, a powerful heat-trapping gas from oil and gas sites, coal mines, livestock and rubbish dumps, must fall at least 25% by 2035, and road transport emissions by 20%. Figure 4. What has to be cut, and by how much. There is progress to build on. In 2025 renewables generated more of the world’s electricity than coal for the first time, and solar power has been built seven times faster than forecast a decade ago. Before the Paris Agreement, the world was on course for almost 4°C of warming. For Africa, the gap between cause and harm is stark. The world’s least developed countries, many of them African, produce just 3% of global emissions, about 1.5 tonnes a person against a world average of 6.4 tonnes and 17.6 tonnes for each American. Figure 5. Greenhouse gas emissions per person, 2025.

items.title: Jeunes entrepreneurs : 200 milliards FCFA pour débloquer les financements
items.description: © DR En marge de la 12e édition du Cameroon Business Forum à Douala, le Gouvernement a mis les jeunes et les femmes au cœur des réformes du financement. Une ligne de crédit de 200 milliards de FCFA et la garantie de l'État doivent permettre de transformer les bonnes idées en entreprises viables et créatrices d'emplois. Comment faciliter l'accès au financement pour les jeunes et les femmes qui veulent entreprendre ? C'est l'une des questions au cœur de l'atelier consacré à l'innovation, l'incubation d'entreprises et aux start-up portées par les jeunes et les femmes, organisé en marge de la 12e édition du Cameroon Business Forum, à Douala. Autour de cet enjeu, les échanges ont réuni Louis Paul Motaze, Ministre des Finances, Achille Bassilekin III, Ministre des Petites et Moyennes Entreprises, de l'Économie sociale et de l'Artisanat, et Henri Eyebe Ayissi, Ministre des Domaines, du Cadastre et des Affaires foncières, qui assurait la modération. Pour Louis Paul Motaze, faciliter l'accès au crédit suppose aussi de mieux préparer les entrepreneurs. Un projet bien structuré, un dossier solide et une bonne compréhension des exigences des banques augmentent les chances d'obtenir un financement. Le ministre a notamment évoqué une ligne de crédit de 200 milliards de FCFA destinée à soutenir les jeunes et les femmes entrepreneurs. Il a également expliqué le rôle que peut jouer la garantie de l'État lorsqu'un projet est jugé viable par une banque, mais que son promoteur ne dispose pas de garanties suffisantes ou inexistantes. Le principe est clair : aider les bons projets à accéder au financement, tout en veillant à leur qualité et à leur adéquation avec les priorités du Gouvernement. « Nous ne faisons pas la promotion de la médiocrité, mais de ce qui est bon », a souligné le Ministre des Finances. Au-delà du financement, les participants ont mis en avant plusieurs leviers : la formation des entrepreneurs, l'incubation, l'innovation, l'accompagnement technique et une meilleure diffusion de l'information sur les mécanismes de soutien disponibles. Faire connaître les dispositifs existants, c'est aussi faciliter l'accès au financement. L'enjeu est de donner aux jeunes et aux femmes les moyens de transformer leurs idées en entreprises viables, créatrices de richesses et d'emplois. Un pari économique majeur pour le Cameroun, où les jeunes et les femmes représentent le principal vivier entrepreneurial, mais restent les plus exclus du crédit bancaire classique. Cet article Jeunes entrepreneurs : 200 milliards FCFA pour débloquer les financements est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: BEAC-Inde : Yvon Sana Bangui renforce la diplomatie monétaire de la CEMAC
items.description: © DR En marge de la Conférence internationale des Gouverneurs des Banques centrales, le Gouverneur de la BEAC a rencontré son homologue de la Reserve Bank of India. Une rencontre stratégique pour moderniser les paiements en CEMAC et affirmer le poids diplomatique de la Banque centrale. La CEMAC s'ouvre aux puissances émergentes. Le Gouverneur de la Banque des États de l'Afrique Centrale (BEAC), M. Yvon Sana Bangui, a rencontré son homologue de la Reserve Bank of India (RBI) à New Delhi, le 20 octobre 2026, en marge de la Conférence internationale des Gouverneurs des Banques centrales. Cette rencontre s'inscrit dans la volonté de la BEAC de renforcer la coopération technique et le partage d'expériences avec les banques centrales des pays émergents. Les échanges entre les deux Gouverneurs ont plus particulièrement porté sur la modernisation des systèmes de paiement et l'inclusion financière. À cet égard, l'expérience de la RBI en matière d'infrastructures de paiement instantané, d'interopérabilité et d'inclusion financière de masse a été présentée comme une référence utile pour la BEAC. La coopération entre la BEAC et la RBI constitue en elle-même un signal politique fort. Elle témoigne de la crédibilité internationale de la BEAC, de son ouverture aux meilleures pratiques et de sa capacité à dialoguer avec les grandes banques centrales. Les deux institutions ont convenu d'explorer les voies d'une coopération technique concrète, notamment dans les domaines des systèmes de paiement, de la cybersécurité financière, de l'intelligence artificielle et des swaps de devises. Le Gouverneur de la BEAC a rappelé que cette dynamique s'inscrit dans la stratégie d'ouverture de la BEAC vers les banques centrales des pays émergents, à l'image des conventions déjà signées avec plusieurs banques centrales. Il a également évoqué son engagement au sein de l'Association des Banques Centrales Africaines et de l'Institut Monétaire Africain. Les équipes techniques des deux institutions se rapprocheront dans les prochaines semaines afin d'identifier les domaines prioritaires et les modalités de ce partenariat. Les deux Gouverneurs ont convenu de maintenir un dialogue régulier. Cet article BEAC-Inde : Yvon Sana Bangui renforce la diplomatie monétaire de la CEMAC est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: Public frustration with elected leaders could fuel military coups in Africa – Yemi Osinbajo
items.description: Former Nigerian Vice President Yemi Osinbajo has warned that growing public tolerance for military coups in Africa reflects frustration with elected leaders who abuse power, weaken constitutional institutions and undermine democratic principles. Speaking at the third Good Governance Africa Annual Lecture, held under the theme Democracy Under Pressure: Rebuilding Trust, Accountability and Institutional Integrity in Africa’s New Political Era , Mr Osinbajo said the trend should prompt a serious examination of the failures of elected governments. Citing an Afrobarometer report indicating that 53% of Africans would accept military intervention if elected leaders abused their power, he cautioned against interpreting such sentiments as support for military dictatorship. “A coup is an attack, of course, on constitutional government, but the conditions in which coups occur also demand honest reflection,” he said. “They often follow profound failures in security, accountability, and public confidence.” Mr Osinbajo added that some elected leaders had themselves weakened constitutional rule by manipulating political rules or restricting opportunities for genuine political change. His remarks come amid concerns about political instability, public discontent and the resurgence of military takeovers in parts of Africa. Good Governance Africa said the lecture was organised against a backdrop of rising protests, political dissatisfaction and violence across the continent. GGA seeks answers to growing democratic discontent Tina Asante-Apeatu, Executive Director of Good Governance Africa’s West Africa Regional Office, said the organisation convened the forum to examine whether growing dissatisfaction with democracy represented a rejection of democratic governance itself or concerns about how it was being practised. “Research is showing more and more people are complaining,” she said. “People are complaining of democracy, protest, violence here and there, not only in Ghana but in Africa.” She said the organisation wanted to create a platform for citizens to express their views and help identify the factors driving the growing discontent. “So we thought, listen, let’s bring the conversation back on board. Let the citizens know, or let’s hear from the citizens,” she said. “Is it really that they are fed up with democracy as we know it, or is it that misinformation and disinformation is playing a part here?” Ms Asante-Apeatu said the forum was intended to stimulate public discussion and bring citizens and experts together to better understand the challenges confronting democratic governance. “So we decided to bring this conversation up to trigger the conversation from ordinary people. I mean, hearing from the experts so we know what is actually happening,” she added. Discussions at the lecture also focused on the abuse of authority and the need to strengthen accountability, with panelists drawn from governance institutions, the legal profession, security services, civil society and research institutions. One panelist described the prevailing circumstances as a major security threat, highlighting the links between democratic governance, political stability and public confidence in state institutions. Participants also highlighted the need for more participatory democracy, arguing that citizen involvement should extend beyond elections and occasional public consultations to give people a meaningful role in governance and decision-making. The concerns raised at the lecture point to a challenge facing African democracies: rebuilding public trust in elected institutions while protecting constitutional rule against both authoritarian leadership and military intervention.

items.title: UFOA-A U20 : Un échec aux causes multiples pour les Aiglons
items.description: © Internet Éliminés après seulement deux rencontres du tournoi UFOA-A U20 2026, les Aiglons ne participeront pas à la prochaine Coupe d’Afrique des Nations de la catégorie. Au-delà des insuffisances constatées sur le terrain, cette désillusion suscite des interrogations sur les choix techniques et les critères de sélection des joueurs. Deux matchs, deux défaites sur le même score (0-1) et aucun but inscrit. Le bilan des Aiglons dans le tournoi qualificatif organisé à Bamako est loin des ambitions affichées. Battus par la Guinée le 15 octobre, puis par la Gambie trois jours plus tard, les hommes de Mamoutou Kané dit Mourlé ont prématurément abandonné leurs espoirs de qualification. Sur le terrain, les difficultés offensives ont particulièrement pesé. Face aux Guinéens comme face aux Gambiens, les Juniors maliens ont éprouvé des difficultés à construire leurs actions et à déséquilibrer les défenses adverses. Malgré les changements opérés par le staff technique, l’équipe n’a jamais réussi à trouver la solution. Des choix qui interrogent Outre les insuffisances techniques et tactiques, cette élimination ravive le débat sur la composition des sélections nationales de jeunes. Certains observateurs s’interrogent sur les critères de choix des joueurs et sur la place accordée aux performances individuelles en clubs et dans les académies. Toutefois, les résultats décevants ne permettent pas, à eux seuls, de conclure que les meilleurs éléments ont été écartés. La constitution d’une sélection répond également à des exigences de complémentarité, d’équilibre entre les postes et d’adaptation au projet de jeu du sélectionneur. Après la défaite contre la Gambie, Mamoutou Kané a assumé sa responsabilité dans l’élimination, tout en défendant ses choix. « Oui, je suis le principal responsable de cette élimination du Mali. Je ne regrette pas mes choix, l’équipe avait toute ma confiance », a déclaré le technicien qui avait conduit le Mali au sacre à la CAN U20 2019. Cette contre-performance lui a finalement coûté son poste. Dans un communiqué publié le 20 octobre, la FEMAFOOT a annoncé avoir reçu sa démission, à l’issue d’échanges avec le Président du Comité exécutif. L’instance prévoit également une réorganisation de l’encadrement technique et du processus de sélection des équipes nationales de jeunes. Cette nouvelle désillusion, quelques semaines après l’élimination des U17, appelle une réflexion sur les méthodes de détection et de sélection, mais aussi sur la capacité des encadrements techniques à tirer le meilleur parti des talents maliens disponibles.

items.title: Cameroun : saisie d’un important stock de produits pharmaceutiques illicites au marché central de Yaoundé
items.description: © DR La gendarmerie nationale a procédé à la saisie d’un important stock de produits de pharmacie estimé à plusieurs dizaines de millions de FCFA. Une situation qui interpellent encore des acteurs sur le renforcement de la lutte contre le faux médicament et les produits illicites au Cameroun. Le trafic des produits illicites se poursuit au Cameroun bien que les autorités déploient des efforts pour y mettre fin. Cette semaine, au marché central de Yaoundé, les éléments de la Compagnie de gendarmerie de Yaoundé 1 er ont procédé à la saisie d’un important stock de produits pharmaceutiques illicites. L’opération a permis de sortir du circuit de commercialisation, des produits illicites comme le Metamizol, des antibiotiques, des sirops, des perfusions. Tous mal conditionnés et provenant d’origine douteuse, se trouvaient dans des espaces clandestins de conservation. Sur renseignement de la population, les gendarmes ont démantelé le réseau de trafic et interpelé des personnes suspectes. Le stock de produit quant à lui est destiné à la destruction. Cette saisie opérée ramène l’opinion à s’intéresser à la prolifération des produits illicites en général, et des faux médicaments en particulier dans les villes. Ces produits se retrouvent dans des espaces de vente à proximité des rues où ils sont plus accessibles, tout comme ils se vendent dans des circuits noirs et se retrouvent dans des ménages pour consommation. Les effets néfastes sur des personnes, des familles et sur l’environnement sont au bout de la chaine. Les saisies régulières de ces produits démontrent de l’ampleur de la situation et de l’insuffisance des efforts déjà consentis dans le lutte contre le phénomène. Le cas du marché central de Yaoundé survient au cours de la semaine où l’on céblèbre la Journée africaine de lutte contre le faux médicament. Célébrée le 21 octobre, l’édition 2026 avait comme fil conducteur : « Faux médicaments, vrai danger : ensemble, sécurisons la chaîne d’approvisionnement au Cameroun, pour une meilleure Couverture Santé Universelle. » Cette journée a donné l’occasion au ministre de la Santé publique Malachie Manaouda de rappeler que les faux médicaments constituent une menace majeure pour la santé publique. Ils occasionnent des pertes financières. Exposent des patients à des traitements inefficaces, à des complications sanitaires et à la mort. Au sortir de cette célébration, les acteurs impliqués reconnaissent la nécessité de sécuriser davantage la chaîne d’approvisionnement. Il convient aussi de d’améliorer le contrôle de qualité, de renforcer la traçabilité et la surveillance des circuits de distribution pour faciliter l’identification des produits suspects. Cet article Cameroun : saisie d’un important stock de produits pharmaceutiques illicites au marché central de Yaoundé est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: Logeist Group supports Ashanti GJA initiative to honour veteran journalist Kofi Badu
items.description: Logeist Group Limited is supporting the Ashanti Regional Branch of the Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) in its initiative to honour veteran journalist Kofi Badu at the 2026 Ashanti Media Excellence Awards. The recognition is intended to celebrate Mr Badu’s contribution to journalism and his service to the media profession. He currently serves as Chief of Staff at the Manhyia Palace, having built a career in journalism. The Ashanti GJA is using the awards platform to recognise outstanding journalistic work and celebrate individuals whose professional contributions have helped shape the media landscape. The 2026 edition of the awards is scheduled for Saturday, October 24, at the Longford Royal Event Centre, Odeneho Kwadaso, Kumasi, at 6:00 p.m. It will be held under the theme, “Celebrating Excellence, Championing Credibility: Journalism in the Age of AI,” which highlights the importance of professional standards, credibility, and ethical reporting amid the growing influence of artificial intelligence in news production and distribution. The Association is also proposing to institute an annual Kofi Badu Honorary Award for Veteran Journalists to recognise experienced media practitioners whose careers reflect professional dedication, ethical journalism, mentorship and service to society. The proposed award is expected to provide a platform for celebrating veteran journalists and preserving their contributions to the development of the profession for future generations. “For Ashanti GJA, Mr Badu represents a valuable link between generations of journalists. His career offers lessons in professional growth, institutional leadership, innovation and the enduring importance of journalism in national development,” said Kofi Adu Domfeh, Chairman, GJA Ashanti. The support from Logeist Group Limited underscores the role of corporate partnerships in advancing initiatives that promote professional excellence and recognise contributions to public service. The Ashanti GJA continues to position the Media Excellence Awards as a platform for encouraging quality journalism, strengthening professional standards and inspiring the next generation of media practitioners.

items.title: Asian football makes U-turn, endorses Infantino re-election
items.description: The head of Asian football on Friday said the region supported Gianni Infantino’s bid for re-election as FIFA president, weeks after stinging criticism over his aborted World Cup selloff plan. The 56-year-old Swiss was present at a Tokyo meeting of the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) when president Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim al-Khalifa gave his unequivocal backing, in a significant boost to Infantino’s prospects of extending his reign. The AFC in August had joined European body UEFA and CONCACAF, representing federations in North and Central America and the Caribbean, in condemning Infantino over his plan to open FIFA’s premium competitions such as the World Cup to private investors. Infantino has faced calls to quit and lost the support of some associations in his bid to be re-elected to a fourth and final term. “I think that we reaffirm our full commitment, of course, to supporting you and your leadership as you seek a new mandate as FIFA president,” said Sheikh Salman. “I think you’ve visited a lot of countries in Asia. I’ve spoken to a lot of members within this continent. “I know your feeling and I think your commitment is clear as well. Your support to Gianni is very clear.” Hinting at previous discord, Sheikh Salman told the AFC Extraordinary Congress and Infantino: “Gianni, yes, we had some issues we spoke about in the past. “But let’s not relate the two things together. We need to move forward… football is strongest when we work together.” Infantino, who apologised last week for the failed private investment project, has headed FIFA since 2016 and is running for re-election in March. – Grateful Infantino – In response to the AFC’s backing, Infantino said: “We have seen the transformation that Asian football, and as a consequence world football, has gone through in these years. “It has become truly global. It has become for everyone, and this would not have been possible without a strong, a united, a committed Asia. And for this, I thank you very much.” The deadline for candidates to declare for the election is November 18. No heavyweight candidate has put themselves forward to run against Infantino so far, despite outspoken condemnation, most notably from Europe. Many leading European national associations have withdrawn their support for Infantino over controversies including his close relationship with US President Donald Trump. Two months ago the AFC and Sheikh Salman signalled they could turn on Infantino. A joint letter with UEFA and CONCACAF declared football “belongs to no individual”. “Leadership in football is not a possession. It is not about holding — or demanding — power to be held,” they wrote. “When trust is broken through deception, when an individual places himself above the collective that entrusted him with authority, that duty has been abandoned,” the confederations said. Infantino has received the backing of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) while South American governing body CONMEBOL is largely supportive. The confederations do not vote as blocs and there have been some supportive voices for Infantino from within CONCACAF. AFC members Kuwait and 2022 World Cup hosts Qatar had previously backed him. So too did the football federation of Saudi Arabia, which will host the 2034 World Cup. AFP The post Asian football makes U-turn, endorses Infantino re-election appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Finances publiques : le budget 2026 ajusté pour soutenir la santé
items.description: © Internet Le Conseil national de Transition (CNT) a adopté à l’unanimité, ce jeudi 22 octobre 2026, le projet de loi modifiant le budget de l’État pour l’exercice 2026. Le texte doit notamment contribuer au financement du programme de construction et de transformation de 15 infrastructures sanitaires à travers le pays. Le budget rectifié doit permettre de renforcer le dispositif sanitaire à travers des investissements financés sur ressources nationales. Réunis en séance plénière au Centre international de conférences de Bamako (CICB), les membres du Conseil national de Transition ont approuvé à l’unanimité le projet de loi modifiant la Loi de finances 2026, par 121 voix pour. Défendu par le ministre d’État, ministre de l’Économie et des Finances, Alousséni Sanou, le texte, adopté en Conseil des ministres le 3 juillet dernier, intègre notamment le financement d’un programme portant sur 15 infrastructures sanitaires. Le programme prévoit la transformation des centres de santé de référence (CSRéf) des six communes de Bamako en hôpitaux de district modernes. Deux nouveaux hôpitaux de district sont également prévus à Kangaba et à Bla. La liste comprend aussi sept hôpitaux régionaux à Koulikoro, San, Koutiala, Bougouni, Dioïla, Nioro et Bandiagara. Ces investissements doivent renforcer les capacités d’accueil et améliorer l’accès aux soins dans plusieurs localités du pays. Le financement de ces infrastructures est assuré sur le budget national. Toutefois, aucune précision n’a été donnée lors de la séance sur le montant global consacré à ces projets ni sur le calendrier de réalisation des travaux. Des exigences de suivi Au cours de l’examen du texte, la Commission des Finances, de l’Économie, du Plan, de la Promotion du Secteur privé et des Industries a formulé deux recommandations à l’endroit du gouvernement. La première porte sur les crédits supplémentaires ouverts par décrets d’avance. La Commission demande aux autorités d’informer sans délai le Parlement de ces ouvertures de crédits, puis de soumettre un projet de loi de finances portant ratification dès l’ouverture de la prochaine session parlementaire, conformément à la loi organique relative aux lois de finances du 15 août 2025. La seconde recommandation concerne les recettes issues de la cession des bâtiments de l’État. La Commission souhaite que la Direction générale de l’administration des biens de l’État (DGABE) produise des états périodiques permettant de suivre les ressources générées par ces opérations. Présidée par Malick Diaw, cette séance plénière s’inscrit dans les travaux de la session ordinaire d’octobre du CNT. L’adoption du texte permet les ajustements budgétaires nécessaires à la poursuite des investissements prévus, notamment dans le secteur de la santé. Joseph Amara Dembélé

items.title: FG to complete records of Nigerian casualties, assets lost during ECOMOG wars
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (Rtd), has disclosed that efforts are ongoing to document remaining records, casualties, and historical assets of the Nigerian military and other personnel who paid the ultimate sacrifice in the ECOMOG operations in Liberia and Sierra Leone, noting that it is aimed at ensuring proper preservation for posterity. Musa reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to immortalising the legacy and sacrifices of the Economic Community of West African States Monitoring Group (ECOMOG). The Minister made the disclosure when he received a delegation of ECOMOG Veterans, led by Major General Ohifeme Ejimai (Rtd), at the Ministry of Defence Headquarters in Abuja. A statement by Leah Katung-Babatunde, SA Media, said the delegation paid the courtesy visit to brief the minister on the group’s activities and ongoing initiatives. General Musa acknowledged the significant human and financial resources Nigeria deployed under ECOMOG, emphasising that personnel who paid the supreme price particularly during peacekeeping missions in Liberia and Sierra Leone will never be forgotten. He assured the delegation that ongoing efforts to document remaining records, casualties, and historical assets would be thoroughly completed to ensure proper preservation for posterity. Earlier on his remarks, Major General Ejimai (Rtd) provided an update on the status of surviving Nigerian ECOMOG veterans, noting their readiness to continue contributing to national development and security. He urged the Ministry to address documentation gaps and consider establishing a dedicated remembrance day to honour the hundreds of Nigerian troops who lost their lives to secure peace and stability in West Africa. The Economic Community of West African States Monitoring Group (ECOMOG) was a formal regional peacekeeping and peace enforcement force created by the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) in 1990. Driven significantly by Nigerian leadership and troops, ECOMOG played a decisive role in restoring constitutional order, protecting civilian populations, and stabilising West Africa during complex regional crises.
